Last week, Apple revealed that its iPad revenue fell 5% year-over-year in the June quarter. A new report places this decline within the broader context of the tablet market in Q2 2026, with details below.

Global tablet shipments decline

According to the latest report from research firm Omdia (cited by MacMagazine), global tablet shipments in Q2 2026 reached 35.5 million units, down 9.9% year-on-year.

The report notes that despite a 7.5% drop in shipments, Apple remained the clear market leader with 13.5 million iPad shipments and a 37.8% market share. Samsung ranked second with 5.8 million shipments and a 16.3% share; Lenovo came third with an 11.1% share; Xiaomi fourth with 8%; and Huawei fifth with 7.7%.

Among the top five vendors, Lenovo was the only brand to record growth, with shipments up 27.1% compared to Q2 2025.

Omdia noted that vendors outside the top five collectively accounted for 19.1% of total shipments, with their overall shipments falling 23.5% year-on-year.

Below is Omdia research manager Himani Mukka's response to the report:

Mukka added that amid ongoing component supply tightness, "vendors find it difficult to fully prioritise their tablet businesses." They expect to "concentrate limited resources on flagship and high-end models, further tilting the product mix toward premium devices."
